summary: Dependency-confusion beacon under @grabcad scope exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a 'Compatibility shim' under the @grabcad scope and exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any property access, allowing builds that import the real @grabcad/preferences-client to succeed. The main entry invokes require('./beacon.cjs').fire() at import time, and package.json wires the same beacon into a postinstall lifecycle script. beacon.cjs POSTs a payload containing the package name, os.hostname(), the install path, process.cwd(), and the Node version to the hardcoded plain-HTTP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The destination is a bare IPv4 on a non-standard port with no relationship to any legitimate publisher infrastructure; the @grabcad scope belongs to a known vendor and the public registry entry is a stub whose only functional effect is the beacon. This is the canonical dependency-confusion reconnaissance pattern: a public squat under an internal/private scope that fires on install and on require to disclose internal hostnames and build paths to an attacker-controlled collector, establishing feasibility for a follow-on payload against installers whose resolver pulls the public package instead of the internal one.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
